raw_recipe.headline: Sweet and Sour Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Sweet and sour sauce made with sugar, vinegar, soy sauce, and ketchup. Delicious with meatballs and rice or a dipping sauce for spring rolls.

video.description: Learn how to make the perfect sweet and sour sauce with this easy-to-follow video. This versatile sauce is a delicious blend of tangy and sweet flavors, perfect for pairing with chicken, pork, shrimp, or as a dipping sauce.
video.name: How to Make Sweet and Sour Sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Place sugar, water, vinegar, soy sauce, cornstarch, and ketchup in a medium saucepan and bring to a boil. Stir continuously until mixture has thickened.

review.reviewBody: As the recipe is written, this is a good sauce. I did do a few things to doctor my version of the sauce which I think gave it more body and flavor. I used the recipe with these substitutions: 1/4 C of brown sugar and 1/2 C of white sugar instead of 3/4 C white sugar, 1/4 C of pineapple juice instead of water, 1/4 C of ketchup instead of the 1 tablespoon (trust me on this!), and I used 2 Tablespoons of flour dissolved into a little water. I added the flour/water mixture to the boiling (on low heat) mix of the other items. I thought these substitutions brought more body, flavor, and color.

I make this all the time and have passed the recipe around to many. I have followed all the suggestions left by others at different times and no matter what I have done to this recipe, it turns out great! We put chicken in it, or ground beef, or meatballs and serve it over rice. I have added veggies also. You can't go wrong. It is wonderful!

This was awesome and so simple when you're pressed for time! I made it in a large saucepan, increased the ketchup to 1/4 cup, chopped up a green pepper along with 1/2 a pineapple with the juices, threw them in with it, turned it down to low; defrosted a 1 pound bag of frozen jumbo shrimp, tossed it with some cornstarch and fried it over high heat in 1 tablespoon of oil in small batches, throwing them in with the sauce as I went; steamed some rice while cooking the rest of it. Dinner in 30 minutes. Yum!

This is an excellent sauce for egg rolls. I have made a couple of times now. I use 2/3 cup sugar instead 3/4 cup and 1 1/2 tablespoon corn starch instead 2 tablespoon. Try this: Mix everything till the sugar is dissolved. Than pour in to a ice cube tray and freeze. After they are frozen place in a freezer bag. Place 1 or 2 frozen cubes in a microwave safe bowl and cook for about 90 seconds stirring every 30 seconds until thick.

I used this as a base. I used brown sugar and more soy and tomato sauce (not ketchup in Australia). I added a small can of pineapple pieces and the juice and a can of diced capsicums (red peppers to Americans). Once it thickened I turned it off and added the chopped leftover store bought chicken and served it with microwave coconut rice. It was delicious.

This was really good. I first stir fried an onion, a bell pepper, pineapple chunks and 3 cloves of crushed garlic with a little olive oil. Then stired in the cornstarch and the rest of the ingredients. Put it with chicken and it was perfect!

I did the recommendations from one of the users. Use these substitutions: 1/4 cup of brown sugar and 1/2 cup of white sugar instead of 3/4 cup white sugar, 1/4 cup of pineapple juice instead of water, 1/4 cup of ketchup instead of the 1 tablespoon (trust me on this!). I also only used 1-2 TBSP of soy sauce. These are the other recommendations from the lady that I didn't use but am curious about: use 2 Tablespoons of flour dissolved into a little water. Add the flour/water mixture to the boiling (on low heat) mix of the other items. IF you stick with the cornstarch, use less.

Pretty good. My changes: Substituted rice wine vinegar for the white. Will probably use a little less of it next time. Used pineapple juice instead of water. Used less than 1/2 cup of sugar total, using a little brown sugar along with the white. Came out a little thicker than I'd like for my vegetable stir fry, so I'll cut down on the cornstarch, which I added as a slurry, next time.
This is perfect as is. If you have strong or high quality soy sauce might want to dial it back a bit or it will overpower. I had Kikkoman and will use less next time.

After reading some reviews, I followed the suggestions from others and the sauce turned out fantastic. I will no longer buy sweet and sour sauce at the store, this is an easy recipe. I tend to double the batch and store some in the fridge so it is available when I am needing a dipping sauce. Here is the recipe that I use.... 1/4 C of brown sugar 1/2 C of white sugar 1/3 cup white vinegar 1/4 C of pineapple juice and pineapple chunks 1/4 C of ketchup 1/4 cup soy sauce If it is too thin then add a little flour to help give it some body. Boil on the stove and let cool, it will thicken as it cools. This is more of a sweet version of the sauce, if too sweet then reduce the amount of pineapple juice and/or sugar.

Really a great recipe, made the double batch and added some extra vinegar to cut the sweetness and give it a more tangy taste. Made it a few times and just made it into a creamy sauce by adding some cream and milk, super delicious plain and when something is added, definitely a crowd pleaser with fried chicken 10/10 would recommend
Something was way to wrong with this sauce.
Easy to put together and delicious. I grated some orange rind into it to kick up the flavour.
Loved this. Way better than the bought stuff, and super easy to make.
My mom taught me this recipe growing up. I just had to look it up to teach my grandchildren. Love it. It's exactly the recipe my mom taught me. She'd put it over pork chops and rice. Mmmmm

Very easy to make. I did cut back the white sugar and added 2 Tablespoons honey. I also increased to a 1/4 cup ketchup which gives it a dark deep red color because of the soy sauce. This sweet sauce was the perfect addition to my rice and ham dinner. I will use the leftover sauce on breaded chicken fingers I will make in a few days.
Added pineapple juice to the sauce instead of water
no changes perfect!
Easy peasy sauce
Delicious! No substitutes.
